title: AI Red Teaming & Adversarial Testing
interviewAnswer: Red teaming deliberately searches for failure modes outside normal test cases: prompt injection, harmful outputs, data leakage, jailbreaks, tool misuse and robustness failures. I convert discovered attacks into repeatable regression tests.
why: Average-case evaluation misses exactly the weird inputs attackers and real users will discover.
intuition: Test the system like someone actively trying to make it fail, then preserve those failures as permanent tests.
deepDive: Red teaming combines automated attack generation, curated scenarios and human exploration. Severity depends on capabilities and context; a harmless chatbot and an agent with write access need different threat models.
workedExample: For a tool-using assistant, test malicious document instructions, malformed tool arguments, repeated retries, cross-tenant data requests and attempts to bypass confirmation.
commonMistakes: Treating red teaming as a one-off demo before launch.
followUps: How is red teaming different from normal evaluation?
How do you prioritize discovered issues?
production: Run security/evaluation suites before model/prompt/tool changes are promoted, and track risk regressions like software bugs.
